question: The compound interest on a sum at 18 % p.a. for 1frac12years, compounded yearly, is ₹2 862. Find the principal.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate for the 1st year = 18%

Effective rate for the next 1/2 year = 18% ÷ 2 = 9%

Total effective Compound Interest % = 18 + 9 + (18 × 9) / 100 = 28.62%

According to the question, 28.62% of Principal = ₹2862

Principal = (2862 ÷ 28.62) × 100 = 10000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹2862

Rate of Interest (R) = 18% p.a.

Time (T) = 1.5 years

**Formula Used:**

For time = n + f years (where n is the complete year and f is the fraction), compounded yearly:

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ × (1 + fR/100)

Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

**Calculations:**

⇒ Amount (A) = P × (1 + 18/100) × (1 + (1/2 × 18)/100)

⇒ A = P × (118/100) × (109/100)

⇒ A = P × 1.18 × 1.09

⇒ A = 1.2862 P

⇒ CI = A − P = 1.2862 P − P = 0.2862 P

⇒ 0.2862 P = 2862

⇒ P = 2862 ÷ 0.2862

⇒ P = 10000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fractional Year Compounding

When time is given in fractions (e.g., n full years and f fraction of a year), interest for the fractional year is applied as simple interest on the compounded amount: A = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ × (1 + fR/100).

Effective Interest Rate

For two successive periods with different rates R₁ and R₂, the net effective rate is given by the formula: R₁ + R₂ + (R₁ × R₂) / 100.

Half-Yearly & Quarterly Compounding

If compounded half-yearly, the rate becomes R/2 and the time periods become 2T. If quarterly, the rate is R/4 and the time is 4T.
